issues.body: require_one_side_bound remains a standalone public helper whose documentation says a caller should run it before wire::derive_grants. No changed production boundary invokes it, and the acceptance suite calls the helper directly rather than submitting an unseeded controller-authored rule through the real admission path. Consequently, callers can still pass unseedable .acr text directly to derive_grants despite the fail-closed guard language.
issues.fix_hint: Enforce require_one_side_bound at the single shared boundary before controller-authored rule text reaches derive_grants/evaluation, propagate denial fail-closed, and add an integration test showing an unseeded .acr rule is rejected through that real path while a seeded rule succeeds. Otherwise consistently narrow all documentation to an optional static-analysis helper and state that operational enforcement remains unresolved.
issues.title: Fail-closed seeding guard remains unenforced on the real .acr path

issues.body: is_var still recognizes only terms beginning with '?', and term_bound therefore treats a blank-node label such as '_:x' as a bound constant. In an N3 rule formula, that label is formula-scoped/existential rather than an externally fixed endpoint, so it cannot conservatively provide the constant-side lookup claimed by the one-side-bound analysis. A body like `{ _:x p:linkedTo ?o } => { ?o p:ok p:v }` can still pass incorrectly.
issues.fix_hint: Treat blank-node labels as formula-scoped unbound terms for seeding analysis, or reject them as unsupported. Add a require_one_side_bound regression test proving that a blank-node-labelled endpoint cannot seed an otherwise unbound atom.
issues.title: Blank-node labels are still incorrectly accepted as constant seeds

verdict.summary: Round 3 is stagnant. Both round-2 major findings remain: require_one_side_bound is still an optional helper that callers are merely instructed to invoke before wire::derive_grants, with no enforcement at the real controller-authored .acr admission boundary and no integration test through that path. Blank-node labels such as _:x are still treated as bound constants because is_var recognizes only '?' variables, so formula-scoped existential endpoints can incorrectly seed an atom. The updated prose narrows some claims to static analysis, but still describes the helper as a fail-closed guard for controller-authored rules without making refusal operational.
